$comment: THE CASES AN EXPECTATION NAMES BY NAME.
Some student expectations do not just say what to do; they name the hard
cases that make the doing worth a credit. A.5(B) says "solve linear
inequalities in one variable, INCLUDING those for which the application of
the distributive property is necessary and for which variables are included
on both sides". A node whose four forms produce neither of those has not
taught A.5(B) at core, however well it teaches what it does teach.
One shipped node claimed exactly that, at core, with no caveat, while its
own sibling said in writing on the same graph that it was the only node in
the course where both named cases are met. The two claims sat eighty lines
apart, contradicting each other, through every gate in the build — because
every gate asks whether a claim is WELL FORMED, and none of them generated
the items and read them against the words of the standard.
HOW TO READ A CASE.
text      the words the expectation itself uses. CHECKED against the
expectation's own `text` on every run, so a case cannot be
invented here: if the words are not the standard's, the gate
refuses to run at all.
detector  a function in tools/check-named-cases.mjs. Regular expressions
live in the tool and not in this file, because a regular
expression in a content file is a content file nobody reviews.
side      where the case counts. `stem` for an expectation whose verb is
SOLVE or SIMPLIFY — the case is a property of what the learner
is handed. `answer` for one whose verb is WRITE, because a form
that PRINTS Ax + By = C and asks for y = mx + b has not written
it. `either` where both readings are the same act.
says      what a caveat has to say for this case to count as disclosed.
A caveat may also name ALL of an expectation's cases at once — "the two
cases A.5(B) names by name are still absent" tells a reader precisely what
is missing without listing it twice. That idiom is COLLECTIVE in
tools/check-named-cases.mjs, one pattern for every expectation, because it
is a fact about English and not about any one standard.

A.5(B).text: solve linear inequalities in one variable, including those for which the application of the distributive property is necessary and for which variables are included on both sides; and
